title: Anandibai Ityadi Galpa (Anandibai and Other Stories)

access.edition_or_version: First edition, 1957 (Bengali); Sahitya Akademi Award for Bengali, 1958
access.translator: Various English translations; collection read through English renderings

mechanics.premise: Fifteen comic and satirical stories on love, courtship, family, and politics, in which ordinary situations are pursued with mock-serious logic.
mechanics.reader_promise: Dry, intelligent Bengali comedy: absurd premises handled with a straight, learned narrator.
mechanics.opening: Stories typically open with a plausible domestic or social situation that is then pushed into absurdity by literal-mindedness.
mechanics.point_of_view: A learned, mock-serious narrator who reports absurdity as if it were unremarkable, producing the comic distance identified by Bergson.
mechanics.character_system: Frequently types rather than deep individuals: pedants, clerks, schemers, and eccentrics whose logic is followed to its comic conclusion.
mechanics.conflict_and_stakes: Low external stakes raised by the narrator's gravity; the comedy lies in following a small rule to an absurd limit.
mechanics.structure: The comic short story: a single absurd premise escalated, with a turn or reversal at the close.
mechanics.comic_system: Mock-serious narration, absurd literal-mindedness, understatement, and parody of learned or official registers.
mechanics.dialogue: Period Bengali registers; translation limits claims about idiom and wordplay.
mechanics.setting: Bengali domestic, professional, and small-town life of the early-to-mid twentieth century.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Understatement (D4) and mock-formal inflation (D5); parody of scholarly and bureaucratic discourse.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Plausibility -> absurd escalation -> reversal -> wry close.
mechanics.comic_escalation: Heightens one absurd rule rather than stacking unrelated jokes.
mechanics.climax: The story's logical extreme or reversal.
mechanics.ending: A dry comic turn that exposes the absurdity without moralising.
mechanics.conventions: Draws on Bengali comic and satirical short fiction and on the personal essay tradition.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Brings scientific and lexicographic precision to comedy of logic, making pedantry itself comic material.
mechanics.critical_reception: Basu is widely regarded as the outstanding Bengali humourist of the twentieth century; the collection won a Sahitya Akademi Award (1958).
mechanics.audience_reception: Adapted for film by Satyajit Ray and others; a continuing classroom and popular presence.
mechanics.translation_note: Technique is assessed from English renderings; sound-based wordplay and idiom are not claimed.
